title: In what order do we build a rectangle from its diagonal angles?
description: A rectangle is built step by step so that its diagonal cuts one corner into sixty degrees and thirty degrees. Keeko's doubt is that the sixty degree angle can be drawn at the other end of the side, and the video breaks it.
teaching_notes: One idea: only the angles are given, so the side is drawn first, then the angle at the end where the diagonal starts, and the perpendiculars finish the rectangle. Watch for students who draw the set angle at the wrong end of the side.

source: Construct a rectangle in which one of the diagonals divides
video_script.why: A learner plans the order of a construction from a rough diagram and builds a rectangle whose diagonal makes the angles sixty degrees and thirty degrees at a corner.
video_script.substitution: the book's rectangle ABCD with the diagonal AC, the side AB of any length
video_script.anchor: the book's rectangle ABCD built from the side AB, with the diagonal AC
video_script.wrong_answer: draw the sixty degree angle at bee
video_script.wrong_move: puts the set angle at the end of the side where the perpendicular is, not where the diagonal starts
video_script.payoff_line: The rectangle is ready. The diagonal eigh cee cuts the corner at eigh into sixty degrees and thirty degrees.

final_answer.value: rectangle ABCD with the diagonal AC making 60 degrees with AB and 30 degrees with AD
final_answer.spoken: the rectangle is ready, with the diagonal cutting the corner into sixty degrees and thirty degrees

maths_rules: each corner of a rectangle is 90 degrees
60 degrees + 30 degrees = 90 degrees, so the corner at A is cut into 60 and 30
the side AB can have any length, since only the angles are given
D lies on the perpendicular to AB through A and on the perpendicular to BC through C
video_script.design: A rough rectangle ABCD stays at the side. The construction is drawn on the board in four steps, each new line in a new colour.

beats.on_screen: title card, then a rough rectangle ABCD with the line from A to C and the two angles at A marked 60 degrees and 30 degrees

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the rough rectangle ABCD is drawn
marks.angles: the line from A to C is drawn and the two angles at A are marked

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about building a rectangle eigh bee cee dee.
<bookmark mark='angles'/>The line from eigh to cee must cut the corner at eigh into sixty degrees and thirty degrees.
In what order should its parts be drawn?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the rough diagram of ABCD stays; a small right angle is drawn where two lines meet and labelled perpendicular

marks.rough: the rough diagram of the rectangle stays on the board as the plan
marks.perp: a right angle is marked where two lines meet and the word perpendicular is written

narration: <bookmark mark='rough'/>A rough diagram helps us plan the order of the drawing.
<bookmark mark='perp'/>A line that meets another line at a right angle is called perpendicular to it.

beats.on_screen: Given: rectangle ABCD; the diagonal AC cuts the corner at A into 60 degrees and 30 degrees
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a rectangle eigh bee cee dee. The diagonal eigh cee cuts the corner at eigh into sixty degrees and thirty degrees.

marks.find: the task is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to construct this rectangle.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: draw AB of any length, then a perpendicular at B (90 degrees)

marks.side: the side AB is drawn with any length
marks.perp: a perpendicular line is drawn upwards at B

narration: <bookmark mark='side'/>Step one, draw eigh bee of any length, because only the angles are given.
<bookmark mark='perp'/>Then draw a perpendicular at bee.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: at A draw an angle of 60 degrees with AB; where the ray meets the perpendicular from B, mark C

marks.angle: the protractor draws a ray at 60 degrees from A
marks.cee: the point C is marked where the ray meets the perpendicular

narration: <bookmark mark='angle'/>Step two, at eigh draw an angle of sixty degrees with eigh bee, using the protractor.
<bookmark mark='cee'/>Mark cee where this ray meets the perpendicular from bee.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: through A draw a line perpendicular to AB; the corner at A is now 60 degrees + 30 degrees

marks.line: a perpendicular to AB is drawn upwards through A
marks.split: the corner at A shows 60 degrees and 30 degrees

narration: <bookmark mark='line'/>Step three, draw a line through eigh perpendicular to eigh bee, because dee must lie on it.
<bookmark mark='split'/>The corner at eigh is now cut into sixty degrees and thirty degrees.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: draw a perpendicular to BC at C; D is where it meets the line through A; join C to D

marks.dee: a perpendicular to BC is drawn at C and D is marked where it meets the line through A

narration: <bookmark mark='dee'/>Step four, draw a perpendicular to bee cee at cee. Mark dee where it meets the line through eigh.
<bookmark mark='join'/>Join cee to dee.

beats.on_screen: Answer: rectangle ABCD is ready; AB = CD, AD = BC and every angle is 90 degrees

marks.res: the equal opposite sides are ticked and the four right angles are marked

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The rectangle is ready. The diagonal eigh cee cuts the corner at eigh into sixty degrees and thirty degrees.
<bookmark mark='res'/>Opposite sides are equal, and every angle is ninety degrees.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the finished rectangle
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a speech bubble 'draw the sixty degree angle at B' struck out; the corner at B shows a right angle and the diagonal starting at A

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble appears beside the corner at B
marks.fix: the right angle at B is marked and the diagonal is shown starting at A
marks.keep: the bubble is struck out and the 60 degrees is marked at A

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks we should draw the sixty degree angle at bee, because the perpendicular is there.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the corner at bee is already a right angle, and the diagonal does not start there.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>The diagonal starts at eigh, so the sixty degrees goes at eigh.
